sentences.text: Researchers used live electrical recording methods to study the spinal cords of mice with a specific model of atopic dermatitis, finding that these animals exhibited spontaneous electrical activity absent in healthy controls. Detailed measurements revealed that neurons in the affected mice displayed more excitatory signals and fewer inhibitory signals than normal.

This spontaneous activity ceased when a drug blocking glutamate receptors was applied, yet it persisted with drugs targeting gastrin-releasing peptide or natriuretic peptide receptors, even though tissue tests showed elevated levels of gastrin-releasing peptide and microglia markers. The authors suggest that an imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory signals in the spinal cord contributes to the heightened sensitivity to itch seen in this chronic condition.
The authors state that this is the first study to directly show changes in the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals in a mouse model of chronic itch.
